inline_comments.comment: Missing `assert` keyword. The line `vib_data_dict['indices'] == n3_vibdata._indices` evaluates a boolean comparison and silently discards the result. This is a no-op — the `indices` field is never actually validated. This is particularly significant because verifying what `todict()` stores in `indices` is the central correctness property of the bug fix. Replace with `assert (vib_data_dict['indices'] == n3_vibdata._indices).all()` (or use `assert_array_equal`), and also add a case that checks `vib_data_dict['indices'] is None` when indices match the constraint-derived default (mirrors the old `assert vib_data_dict['indices'] is None`).

`fixture_n3_vibdata` mutates the shared `n3_data` dict in place (`n3_data['hessian'] = h`). Because pytest's function-scoped fixtures share the same object instance within a single test invocation, any test that requests both `n3_data` and `n3_vibdata` (e.g. `test_todict`) will see a mutated `n3_data['hessian']`. This makes the assertion `assert_array_almost_equal(vib_data_dict['hessian'], n3_data['hessian'])` in `test_todict` compare the trimmed hessian against itself rather than against the original full hessian, masking potential bugs. Use a local variable instead: `h = n3_data['hessian'][indices][..., indices, :]` and pass `h` directly to `VibrationsData` without reassigning `n3_data['hessian']`.

`TestDictMethods.test_dict_indices` removes the hessian-resizing step that was present in the old test (`vib_data_dict['hessian'] = hessian[:n_active, :, :n_active, :]`). The new design only works correctly if `@pytest.mark.parametrize('indices, expected_mask', ...)` causes the `n3_vibdata` fixture to be built with the same `indices` value (so the stored hessian is already the right size when `fromdict` is called). Whether pytest's parametrize marker overrides the class-level `fixture_indices` fixture for transitive fixture dependencies is non-obvious and can be version-dependent. This should either be documented with an explicit comment, or the test should be restructured to not rely on this interaction — for example, by explicitly building a `VibrationsData` with the correct-sized hessian in the test body rather than depending on the `n3_vibdata` fixture.

In `test_dos` (and similarly `test_pdos`), `n3_vibdata.get_energies()` is called inside the `pytest.warns(ComplexWarning)` block. However, `get_energies()` is a cached property; the first call (inside the `with` block) caches the result. Any additional warning-generating calls after the block exits will succeed silently. More importantly, placing both the warning-producing call and the subsequent data extraction inside the `with` block means the warning context is broader than necessary. It is cleaner to call `get_energies()` outside the `with` block and use `pytest.warns` only around the specific call that raises the warning.

The changelog entry references private attributes `_indices` and `_atoms` directly. ASE project rules state that changelog entries must not mention private or internal implementation details (those prefixed with an underscore). Rewrite in terms of the public API and user-observable behavior, e.g.: `:meth:`.VibrationsData.todict` previously raised a `ValueError` when `indices` specified a proper subset of atoms; it now correctly serializes the indices in that case.`

The changelog fragment still contains 38 lines of the commented-out section template (I/O, Calculators, Optimizers, etc.). Per ASE scriv conventions, all unused commented-out sections should be deleted, leaving only the active `Bugfixes` section.

The fix changes the comparison target from `range(len(self._atoms))` (all atoms) to `self.indices_from_constraints(self._atoms)` (atoms free of constraints). These are equivalent only when the atoms object has no constraints, so this is a semantic change for constrained systems: `todict()` now returns `indices=None` whenever `_indices` matches the constraint-derived defaults, rather than only when it includes every atom. This is the correct behavior for round-tripping through `fromdict`, but the intent of the change is not documented. A brief inline comment explaining why `indices_from_constraints` is used instead of `range(len(self._atoms))` would prevent future readers from reverting this to the simpler (but buggy) form.

general_comments.comment: The regression test for the actual bug (crash when `1 != len(indices) != len(atoms)`) is exercised only indirectly: `TestDictMethods.test_todict` calls `n3_vibdata.todict()` with a partial-index `n3_vibdata` (e.g., `indices=[0]`), which would have crashed under the old code. The crash prevention is therefore verified. However, because the `indices` assertion is missing (see separate comment), the correctness of the returned value is not verified when the fix applies. Ideally, a dedicated, clearly named test (e.g., `test_todict_with_partial_indices`) should exist that builds a `VibrationsData` with `len(indices) < len(atoms)` and no constraints, calls `todict()`, and explicitly asserts both that no exception is raised and that the `indices` key in the returned dict contains the expected array. This would make the regression test self-documenting.

The PR replaces the entire `n2` fixture set (N2 diatomic) with an `n3` fixture set (N3 triatomic). While the motivation is sound (the bug only manifests when `len(indices)` can differ from `len(atoms)` by more than one, requiring at least 3 atoms), all existing tests unrelated to the bug fix are also rewritten to use N3. This creates a large, noisy diff that makes it harder to isolate the bug-fix-specific changes from the incidental test refactoring. Consider separating the refactoring (N2→N3 fixture rename and data update) from the new `TestDictMethods` class into different commits, or at minimum keeping the old N2 fixtures alongside the new N3 ones so that reviewers can focus on what changed.

The new test fixtures and data dicts use inconsistent quote styles within the same file: `fixture_n3_data` and `fixture_n3_unstable_data` use double-quoted key strings (e.g., `"atoms"`, `"hessian"`), while the test functions and the old code use single-quoted strings (e.g., `n3_data['atoms']`). The project's style guideline favors single quotes. Please normalize to single quotes throughout the new additions.

The outer `fixture_indices` fixture (defined at module level with `params=[None]`) and the inner `TestDictMethods.fixture_indices` (with `params=[[], None, [0], [0, 1]]`) create an implicit override that is easy to miss when reading any single test. Since `fixture_n3_vibdata` depends on `indices`, most tests outside `TestDictMethods` only ever run with `indices=None`. This is intentional but undocumented. A short comment on the outer `fixture_indices` (e.g., `# Overridden inside TestDictMethods to exercise partial-index cases`) would make the design explicit.
